challenges.title: Average sensitivity
challenges.summary: The quantity is the universal coefficient C in \mathrm{AS}(f)\le Cd\sqrt n for polynomial threshold functions of degree at most d, with 1\le d\le n and \operatorname{sign}(0)=1. A lower coefficient is better.

challenges.title: Block sensitivity separation
challenges.summary: The quantity is the exponent \alpha in \mathrm{bs}(f)\ge s(f)^{\alpha-o(1)}, for a family of total Boolean functions f with s(f)\to\infty. A higher exponent is better. The sensitivity s(f) is the largest number of single bits that change the value of f when flipped at one input. The block sensitivity \mathrm{bs}(f) is the largest number of disjoint sets of bits that each change the value of f when flipped at one input. Rubinstein’s 1995 construction gives \alpha=2. Huang’s 2019 theorem, with Tal’s refinement, gives \mathrm{bs}(f)\le s(f)^4, so \alpha\le4. The OpenAI baseline builds one seed function f with s(f)\le A and block sensitivity \mathrm{bs}(f,0)\ge B at the all-zero input, and composes it with itself, which gives \alpha=\log B/\log A. OpenAI’s Lean proof uses the seed with recursion depth d=9 and size parameter M=9^{10}.

challenges.title: Cap Set Lower Bound in AG(7, 3)
challenges.summary: Construct the largest explicit cap set (no three points collinear) in 7-dimensional affine space over GF(3).

challenges.title: Catalan’s constant
challenges.summary: The quantity is an upper bound on the irrationality exponent \mu(G) of Catalan’s constant. A lower bound is better. The release states irrationality but gives no finite exponent bound; the baseline is the trivial extended-real upper bound +\infty.

challenges.title: CIFAR-10 94% Accuracy Speedrun (Airbench)
challenges.summary: Minimize wall-clock training time to reach 94.0% mean test accuracy on CIFAR-10 using a single 400W NVIDIA A100 GPU.

challenges.title: Circle Packing Sum of Radii in Unit Square (N=26)
challenges.summary: Maximize the sum of radii of N=26 non-overlapping circles packed inside the unit square [0,1]^2.

challenges.title: Contingency-table sampling
challenges.summary: The quantity is the ideal auxiliary-chain inverse-gap upper bound A d^p, where d=10+(m+1)(n+1)\ge10. Lower p is better, with A also tracked. This is an internal bound, not the complete algorithm runtime.

challenges.title: Directed SSSP (Sparse Comparison-Addition)
challenges.summary: Minimize the log-time exponent alpha in O(n (log n)^alpha) for deterministic directed Single-Source Shortest Paths on sparse graphs.

challenges.title: Erdős Minimum Overlap Problem (#36)
challenges.summary: Minimize the maximum overlap constant M for measurable step functions h: [0,2] -> [0,1] with integral 1.

challenges.title: Fourier Transform (Exact DFT)
challenges.summary: Uniform exact arithmetic Discrete Fourier Transform with log-saving exponent kappa in O(n (log n)^(1-kappa)).

challenges.title: Fast 32-bit Integer Sort
challenges.summary: Sort 1,000,000 32-bit integers as fast as possible in pure Python on a fixed-seed dataset.

challenges.title: Spin-one Haldane gap
challenges.summary: The quantity is the uniform periodic spin-one spectral-gap lower bound \gamma_L at J=1, compared on the original domain of even L\ge2304. A higher lower bound is better. The claim assumes the cited OpenAI spatial-transfer identities and certified finite inputs. The extension to every integer L\ge24 is listed under Relevant repos.

baseline.label: OpenAI periodic spin-one Haldane gap log(20)/784

challenges.title: Heilbronn triangle
challenges.summary: The quantity is the saving \eta in \Delta(n)\ge cn^{-2+\eta}. A higher saving is better. The baseline is \eta=2/(45435k+16), where k=T^2+1 and T=\binom{\binom{163}{41}}{3}; the displayed approximation comes from the follow-up. Each claim assumes estimates from the manuscript and states them, with its proof scope.

challenges.title: Integer Multiplication
challenges.summary: Multitape Turing machine integer multiplication below O(n log n), maximizing log-saving kappa in O(n (log n)^(1-kappa)).

baseline.label: Harvey-van der Hoeven O(n log n) (kappa = 0)

challenges.title: Kissing Number in 11 Dimensions
challenges.summary: Maximize the number of non-overlapping unit spheres in R^11 that simultaneously touch a central unit sphere.

challenges.title: 4×4 Complex Matrix Multiplication Tensor Rank
challenges.summary: Minimize the number of scalar multiplications required to multiply two 4x4 complex matrices.

challenges.title: Matrix Multiplication Exponent
challenges.summary: Minimize the asymptotic matrix multiplication exponent omega over complex arithmetic circuits O(n^(omega+epsilon)).

challenges.title: One-sample matroid prophet inequality
challenges.summary: The quantity is the guaranteed fraction of expected offline optimum, with one sample per element of an arbitrary finite matroid and the same almighty full-seed arrival-order adversary. A higher fraction is better. Computation can take exponential time.

challenges.title: Goemans–Williamson Max-Cut SDP Integrality Gap
challenges.summary: Minimize the upper bound on the Max-Cut SDP integrality ratio CUT(G) / SDP(G) by constructing a high-dimensional graph instance.

challenges.title: NanoGPT speedrun
challenges.summary: Train GPT-2 small to 3.28 val loss on FineWeb as fast as possible on 8xH100.

challenges.title: No-Three-In-Line Problem on 32×32 Grid
challenges.summary: Maximize the number of points placed on a 32x32 lattice grid so that no three points are collinear (theoretical ceiling 2N = 64).

challenges.title: Ordered matrix removal
challenges.summary: The quantity is the number of cells rc in a forbidden ordered binary pattern with r rows and c columns that has no polynomial removal bound. The goal is the smallest such pattern, measured in cells. Fewer cells are better. Later repair-distance constants do not change this quantity.

metric.name: r c cells in an r\times c pattern

challenges.title: Primitive-root primes
challenges.summary: The quantity is the power a in the lower bound c_bx/(\log x)^a for primitive-root primes in (x,2x), for the same admissible integer base b. A lower power is better.

baseline.label: OpenAI baseline a <= 2 in c_b x / (log x)^a

challenges.title: Quasi-Riemann hypothesis
challenges.summary: The quantity is the zero-free half-plane threshold \theta for Dirichlet L-functions, which include zeta. A lower threshold is better. The OpenAI paper also covers finite-order Eisenstein Hecke functions over \mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{-3}); claims with Lean prove the Dirichlet theorem only. The claims retain the source proof conditions.

challenges.title: Diagonal Ramsey Number R(5,5) Lower Bound
challenges.summary: Maximize the number of vertices N of a graph with neither a 5-clique K_5 nor an independent set of size 5 (establishing R(5,5) > N).

challenges.title: Salem–Spencer 3-AP-Free Subset of {1..1000}
challenges.summary: Maximize the size r_3(1000) of a subset of {1, 2, ..., 1000} containing no three-term arithmetic progression (x + z = 2y).

challenges.title: Sidorenko counterexample
challenges.summary: The quantity is the nondirect residual constant C in the exponent -D+C. A lower constant is better. This is an internal proof step, conditional on transfer within the source orbit-counting argument. The counterexample still has 35 vertices and 66 edges; this constant does not give the full dimension.

challenges.title: Snaky
challenges.summary: The quantity is the upper bound on Maker moves needed to win Snaky on the infinite square board. Fewer moves are better. Nándor Sieben’s finite 17\times17 strategy, supplied by gotrevor, also works on the infinite board. The separate 15\times15 result concerns board size.

challenges.title: Minimum-Size 17-Wire Sorting Network
challenges.summary: Minimize the total number of comparators S(17) in a compare-and-swap network that sorts all 2^17 binary inputs.

challenges.title: Subset Sum (Randomized Word RAM)
challenges.summary: Minimize the exponential time exponent alpha in O(2^(alpha n)) for exact Subset Sum in the randomized Word RAM model.

challenges.title: Unit-distance final grid
challenges.summary: The quantity is the number of selected edges Nj in the final algebraic-grid proof step. Fewer edges are better. The claim assumes the upstream generic-grid and private-valuation lemmas. The line cases are separate, and no better headline unit-distance exponent is claimed.

baseline.label: OpenAI weak pinned planar distance N*j = 20*5 = 100

challenges.title: Van der Waerden numbers
challenges.summary: The quantity is the coefficient c in W_r(k)>k^{ck\lfloor\log_2r\rfloor}, for sufficiently large k, uniformly in r. A higher coefficient is better. Each claim assumes the upstream OpenAI transfer and states the lemmas it adds. The current region allows every fixed c<1/8; 1/8 is not an attained value.
